title: AppTest: removing input fields on rerun may lead to "We'll never get here" condition in session_state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

In writing tests with AppTest on an existing application (which appears to work correctly in the browser), an unexpected error occurred that appears to be internal to streamlit/AppTest and seems to be labelled as an "impossible" condition in comments.
The example code demonstrates this with a single file. One would need to extract the string into a separate file to try the application through a browser.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

def test_simple():

    at = AppTest.from_string ( """

import streamlit as st

for k, v in [ ('started', False) ]:
    if k not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[k] = v

if not st.session_state.started:

    with st.status('Starting', expanded = True) as s1:

        q1 = s1.text_input('Start', key = 'question_1')

        if len(q1) > 5:

            st.write('ok: started')

            st.session_state.started = True
            st.rerun()

else:

    st.status('Started', state = 'complete', expanded = False )

    with st.status('Question 2', expanded = True) as s2:

        q2 = s2.text_input('Question 2', key = 'question_2')

        if len(q2) > 5:
            st.write('ok: stopping')
            st.stop()

        """ )

    at.run()

    assert at.session_state.started == False

    s1 = at.get('status')[0]

    t1 = s1.get('text_input')[0]

    assert t1.key == 'question_1'

    t1.set_value('aaaaaa')
    t1.run()

    assert at.session_state.started == True

    s2 = at.get('status')[1]

    t2 = s2.get('text_input')[0]

    assert t2.key == 'question_2'

    t2.set_value('bbbbbb')
    t2.run()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

The attached file was run with pytest:

pytest test_simple.py

### Expected Behavior

The test runs without the error.

### Current Behavior

This is the pytest output (minimally edited to remove private information):

    def _getitem(self, widget_id: str | None, user_key: str | None) -> Any:
        """Get the value of an entry in Session State, using either the
        user-provided key or a widget id as appropriate for the internal dict
        being accessed.

        At least one of the arguments must have a value.
        """
        assert user_key is not None or widget_id is not None

        if user_key is not None:
            try:
                return self._new_session_state[user_key]
            except KeyError:
                pass

        if widget_id is not None:
            try:
                return self._new_widget_state[widget_id]
            except KeyError:
                pass

        # old state at the same time, so the order we check is arbitrary.
        # The exception is if session state is set and then a later run has
        # a widget created, so the widget id entry should be newer.
        # The opposite case shouldn't happen, because setting the value of a widget
        # through session state will result in the next widget state reflecting that
        # value.
        if widget_id is not None:
            try:
                return self._old_state[widget_id]
            except KeyError:

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.36.0
- Python version: 3.10.12
- Operating System: WSL2/ubuntu (5.15.146.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2 #1 SMP Thu Jan 11 04:09:03 UTC 2024 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux)
- Browser: n/a (run in AppTest)


### Additional Information

A simpler version of the code that used only the text_input controls did not show the problem. (But it also does not achieve the UI effects intended by the creator of the application.)

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-9128)
I am also having the same error.
[USER] Thanks for reporting this issue. I was able to reproduce it.
Is this issue going to be addressed in the near future? This really breaks my testing strategy. Are there any good workarounds?

Hi! I’d like to investigate this confirmed AppTest failure. I checked the current develop branch, and the reported failure seam still exists: ElementTree.get_widget_states() serialises widgets from the tree, while a removed widget’s value may already have been pruned from session state.
Would you be open to a focused PR that first adds the issue’s rerun/removal regression case, then ensures AppTest no longer tries to serialise a removed widget whose state is unavailable? I would keep broader stale-block, dialog, and fragment behaviour out of scope unless it proves inseparable during reproduction.
